item.title: Lee County retail added 174 jobs through last fall but finished below the previous December
item.description: Stores in Lee County added 174 payroll jobs between October and December 2025, yet finished that holiday season with 134 fewer jobs than a year earlier. The difference matters for readers in Tupelo ahead of Small Business Saturday on Nov. 28. A busy season can lift employment over the fall even when the year-over-year count goes the other way. The Bureau of Labor Statistics counted 6,762 retail jobs in Lee County in October 2025, 6,859 in November and 6,936 in December. December 2024 had 7,070. The later December accounted for roughly 14.5% of all 47,860 private jobs at workplaces in the county. The number of retail establishments was nearly unchanged. Lee County had 523 in the final quarter of 2025, up from 522 in the same quarter of 2024. Average weekly pay for retail work rose from $659 to $703. After the holiday quarter, the January 2026 count stood at 6,560. February brought 6,562 jobs and March 6,469. The figures include small shops and large chains throughout Lee County. They count jobs where the work takes place and do not measure retail sales or this November’s hiring. Source records from the Bureau of Labor Statistics Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages. Lee County 2025q4 county payroll record: https://data.bls.gov/cew/data/api/2025/4/area/28081.csv . Lee County 2024q4 county payroll record: https://data.bls.gov/cew/data/api/2024/4/area/28081.csv . Lee County 2026q1 county payroll record: https://data.bls.gov/cew/data/api/2026/1/area/28081.csv . Small Business Saturday date: https://legacy.sba.gov/article/2026/11/19/sba-encourages-americans-shop-smallr-small-business-saturdayr-november-28 .
item.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics and U.S. Small Business Administration

item.title: Tupelo had 59 more unemployed residents in October as the city’s labor force shrank
item.description: The number of Tupelo residents counted as unemployed rose to 596 in October from 537 in September, a gain of 59. Tupelo’s unemployment rate increased from 3.1% to 3.5%, according to the Mississippi Department of Employment Security. The October city estimates are preliminary and the September figures are revised. These figures are not seasonally adjusted. Employment among Tupelo residents fell by 144, from 16,779 in September to 16,635 in October. The city’s labor force, which includes employed and unemployed residents, declined by 85 to 17,231. That combination explains why unemployment rose even as fewer residents were in the labor force. Lee County, which includes Tupelo, saw its jobless rate climb from 3.0% to 3.4% over the same month. The county figures include the city, so the two counts should not be added. The county recorded 1,261 unemployed residents, up from 1,129. County employment fell from 36,220 to 35,909. The city estimates describe residents of Tupelo. They do not count positions at all businesses located inside the city. Source: Mississippi Department of Employment Security, preliminary October 2026 and revised September 2026 city and county labor-force tables: https://mdes.ms.gov/media/23357/labormarketdata.pdf .
item.source: Mississippi Department of Employment Security, October labor market report

item.title: Tupelo orientation for December high school graduates closes registration Monday
item.description: The Tupelo campus of Itawamba Community College will host December high school graduates on Wednesday, Dec. 2, at 1 p.m. The live sign-up table lists Monday, Nov. 30, as the final registration date for this free session for incoming spring students. It takes place in the Academic and Student Center at 2176 South Eason Blvd. in Tupelo. ICC requires orientation for high school seniors who graduate this December and plan to start college in January. Students may choose Tupelo even if they expect to take classes at the Fulton campus. A second session is at 1 p.m. Thursday, Dec. 3, at the W.O. Benjamin Fine Arts Center in Fulton. Its registration also ends Nov. 30. Both dates were checked on the live registration form on Nov. 26 against the college’s Nov. 4 announcement. Applicants must apply for admission before registering for orientation. Students can arrange a spring class schedule and take their college ID photo during the visit. Parents or guardians can attend. The college encourages students to send ACT scores before orientation. Students changing an existing reservation can use the code in their confirmation email. The orientation office answers questions at orientation@iccms.edu. ICC announcement: https://www.iccms.edu/news/icc-opens-registration-for-december-2026-graduate-orientation . Official sign-up and session details: https://www.iccms.edu/Admissions/Orientation-at-ICC/Orientation-Registration . Admission and orientation instructions: https://www.iccms.edu/Orientation .
item.source: Itawamba Community College, dated announcement and live registration form

item.title: Extreme drought covers nearly two-thirds of Lee County in Nov. 24 assessment
item.description: All of Lee County, including Tupelo, was in severe drought or worse in the November 24 assessment. Extreme drought or worse covered 65.35% of the county, including 1.28% in exceptional drought, the highest category. Two weeks earlier 39.58% was in extreme drought or worse and none was exceptional. The latest percentages matched November 17. These are county area shares, not a reading for every Tupelo household. The percentages are shares of land area. Categories in the U.S. Drought Monitor table are cumulative; the more severe categories are included in the less severe ones. The national map is dated Tuesday, November 24, before Wednesday’s weather. The map does not measure subsequent rainfall. Statewide, extreme drought or worse covered 66.91% of Mississippi on November 24, up from 53.56% the week before. Sources: https://usdmdataservices.unl.edu/api/CountyStatistics/GetDroughtSeverityStatisticsByAreaPercent?aoi=28081&startdate=11/10/2026&enddate=11/24/2026&statisticsType=1 (county area percentages for November 10, 17 and 24); https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/data/png/20261124/20261124_ms_text.png (dated state map and statewide comparison).

item.title: Tupelo career center, Saltillo High and Mooreville Middle appear on TVA's STEM awards list
item.description: Tupelo Career Technical Center — Tupelo Water & Light Department. Saltillo High School — Tombigbee Electric Power Association. Mooreville Middle School — Tombigbee Electric Power Association. TVA groups recipients by the local power company. The workbook places Tupelo Career Technical Center under the Tupelo Water & Light Department. It lists Saltillo High School and Mooreville Middle School under Tombigbee Electric Power Association. Tupelo Public School District identifies its career center as the Tupelo Career-Technical Center. The classroom award list gives no individual grant amounts or descriptions. The district career center also has a separate reference to a robotics grant; the roster does not identify this classroom award as a robotics project. The Tennessee Valley Authority and Bicentennial Volunteers, Inc., its retiree organization, announced the regional awards on November 23, 2026. The 2026–27 list contains 334 school entries across the region, 36 in TVA's Mississippi district. The program awards $1.5 million regionwide and TVA estimates about 96,000 students will benefit across the region. The $5,000 figure is an upper limit for an individual award. It is not the amount awarded to a named school. Eligible schools receive electricity through a local power company served by TVA. The competitive process gives preference to proposals dealing with the environment, energy, economic development or solving community problems. The Tennessee STEM Innovation Network is a program partner and Battelle manages the network. TVA says that since 2018 the partners have provided more than $10.5 million through these awards, supporting more than 940,000 students across the region. Primary award announcement: https://www.tva.com/the-powerhouse/stories/tva-awards--1.5-million-to-support-stem-education-across-the-valley_edu Award program and full recipient list: https://www.tva.com/learn/stem-awards Official workbook: https://tva-azr-eastus-cdn-ep-tvawcm-prd.azureedge.net/cdn-tvawcma/docs/default-source/tva-stem/2026--2027-tva-stem-award.xlsx?sfvrsn=87e985be_1 School district sources: https://www.tupeloschools.com/tctc
